title: Seed compare-none pattern over-matches chained comparisons (silent wrong rewrite)
description: Seed pattern $X == None matches the whole chained-comparison node, so 'x = a == None == b' autofixes to 'x = a is None', silently dropping '== b' — corruption of valid Python. Engine overlap fix (C1) does NOT address this; it is single-rule greediness. Harden the seed pattern (guard against chained comparison) and add a chained-comparison self-test example. Found in final review (I2).

title: CLI silently drops idioms whose rule fails ast-grep compile
description: check.rs uses CompiledIdiom::compile(i).ok() in a filter_map, so a structurally-valid-but-uncompilable rule.pattern passes resolve-time validation then gets silently discarded with no diagnostic. Violates spec sec5/sec10 'fail loud at load'. Fix: compile-check rules at load time (best), or at minimum surface compile errors to stderr instead of .ok()-dropping. Found in final review (I1).

title: .tsx files are not linted (ext_lang maps ts but not tsx)
description: cascade.rs ext_lang maps .ts -> TypeScript but not .tsx, so TypeScript idioms silently do nothing on .tsx (React) files — a large fraction of real TS projects. Note: .tsx likely needs SupportLang::Tsx (separate tree-sitter grammar) and the idiom language-matching must treat typescript/tsx as compatible, so it's not a trivial one-liner. Found in step-7 review (I3).

title: Add a genuinely-safe TypeScript autofix idiom
description: typescript-core currently has zero autofix idioms (triple-equals/optional-chaining were reclassified to warn-and-instruct because their rewrites change behavior). Add a TS idiom whose autofix is mechanically safe — e.g. arrow implicit-return ($P) => { return $E; } -> ($P) => $E, or removing redundant braces — validated by the self-test harness. Also broaden self-test examples to include the unsafe cases (x == null, 0 && 0.x) as negative fixtures. Found in step-7 review (I1).

title: Cascade resolver keys merges by id alone, not (language, id)
description: resolve() groups idiom patches by id across all packs/layers regardless of language. With multiple language packs in base, a Python and a TypeScript idiom sharing an id would wrongly merge into one idiom. Today TS ids are deliberately distinct from Python ids so it's latent, but adding languages or third-party packs makes collisions likely. Fix: key the resolver (and duplicate-id detection) by (language, id). Found while adding the typescript-core pack (step 7).

title: skill-gen emits misleading header for unknown/zero-idiom language
description: render_skill for an unknown language (e.g. 'cobol') or one with no idioms produces a SKILL.md claiming 'X idioms enforced by idiomatic' with body '0 idioms', exit 0 — a build artifact asserting enforcement that doesn't exist. Fix: when support_lang(language) is None or the idiom set is empty, warn to stderr / non-zero, or emit prose that doesn't claim enforcement. Found in agent-loop final review (#3).

title: Decide and test warn-severity exit-code contract for check
description: Spec sec7 says exit codes driven by severity but check only fails on Error; warn and info both exit 0, with no test or comment pinning it. Decide whether an unfixed warn-severity violation fails CI, document the mapping in report(), and add a test. Found in final review (I3).

title: triple-equals detector covers == but not !=
description: The triple-equals idiom's rule pattern '$A == $B' does not match '!=', so 'a != b' (same coercion problem) is undetected. skill_prose says 'never == / !=' but the detector catches only half. Add a second rule arm or a not-equals idiom. Found in step-7 review (I2).
